protocol.transport: MCP over stdio; two real server processes (worldbank + market groups) merged by the client adapter

budget_conditions.clean+1: per-task turn budget = fault-free MCP calibration turns + 1
budget_conditions.clean+4: per-task turn budget = fault-free MCP calibration turns + 4

protocol.budget_anchor_note: per-task turn budget anchored on the **baseline** (middleware-disabled) fault-free turn requirement; the same budget is then used for both arms

server_process_crash.note: the worldbank server process exits abruptly during that call; the stdio session really breaks, the adapter reconnects a fresh process, and the middleware retries the call as a retryable request_error

catalog_drift.note: stale client config advertises an old tool name no server registers; the middleware resolves it against the real catalogue (offline-validated function-name similarity rule)

protocol.calibration: fault-free MCP run per task measured separately with the middleware disabled (baseline_turns) and enabled (guard_turns); the budget sweep anchor is recorded in budget_anchor
protocol.verification: programmatic; ground truth fetched live through the MCP servers before the runs

limitations: The server crash and the catalog drift are deterministic injected scenarios (call #2 of the worldbank server; alias fetch_exchange_rate), not observed production incidents; everything else (stdio transport, process death, reconnects, tool routing, HTTP, LLM) is real.
Single model (deepseek-v4-flash) and repeat seeds vary only the injected fault surface, not model sampling.
A fresh pair of MCP server processes is started per cell, so cold HTTP caches make runs slower and fault assignment depends on the calls the cell actually makes.
MCP stdio needs real pipe handles, so this runner needs full local access; the test suite covers the same adapter logic with the SDK in-memory transport.
Free public APIs are not production grade and API drift can affect reruns.

Measured in both arms: the budget sweep is anchored on the baseline (middleware-disabled) fault-free turn requirement, so the baseline is not held to a guard-calibrated budget (2026-11-24 review P1-2).
